Surah Al-Ahzab [Medinan, and its verses are 73; it was revealed after Al ʿImran]

﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾ persist in His fear (taqwa). ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ in what opposes your sharia (shariʿah, the divine law). ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of what will be before it comes into being, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He creates.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 2:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord﴾, i.e., the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾. And in another reading, it is with the ya' (yā’ taḥtāniyya, the letter ya' pointing below), i.e., ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("they do") instead of ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ ("you do").

And put your trust in Allah ﴿وتَوَكَّلْ عَلى اللَّه﴾ in your affair, ﴿وكَفى بِاللَّهِ وكِيلًا﴾ and Allah is sufficient as a Guardian (wakil), protecting you; and your community (ummah) follows you in all of that.

﴿He has not made for any man two hearts within his body.﴾ This is a refutation of those among the disbelievers who said that he has two hearts, with each of which he understands better than Muhammad (ﷺ) understands. ﴿Nor has He made your wives whom you liken to your mothers' backs (ʾallāʾī tuẓāhirūna)﴾ is read with a hamza and a yāʾ, and without a yāʾ. ﴿Tuẓāhirūna﴾ is read without an alif before the hāʾ, and with it. The second tāʾ is originally assimilated into the ẓāʾ. ﴿Minhunna﴾: a man says, for example, to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother." ﴿Ummahātukum﴾ means "like mothers" in prohibiting her by that statement, which was a form of divorce (ṭalāq) used in the Jāhiliyya (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance). Expiation (kaffāra) is required by it only under its condition, as mentioned in Surat al-Mujādila. ﴿Nor has He made your adopted sons (adʿiyāʾakum, the plural of daʿiyy, one who claims as a son a person who is not his own child)﴾ ﴿your sons﴾ in reality. ﴿That is your saying with your mouths﴾, meaning the Jews and the hypocrites. When the Prophet (ﷺ) married Zaynab bint Jaḥsh, who had been the wife of Zayd ibn Ḥāritha, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had adopted, they said: "Muhammad has married his son's wife." So Allah refuted them in this. ﴿And Allah says the truth﴾ in this matter, ﴿and He guides to the way﴾, the way of truth.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 5:

﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients.﴾ [More just]: more upright (a'dal) ﴿in the sight of Allah.﴾ ﴿But if you do not know their fathers, then [they are] your brothers in religion and your clients.﴾ [Your clients]: your cousins (banu 'ammikum). ﴿And there is no blame upon you for what you have made an error in﴾ concerning that, ﴿but [blame is upon you for] what your hearts have intended﴾ in it, meaning after the prohibition. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what was said by you before the prohibition, ﴿Merciful﴾ to you in that matter.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 33, Verse 6:**

﴿The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves﴾ in what he calls them to, and their own selves call them to opposition to it. ﴿And his wives are their mothers﴾ in the prohibition of marrying them. ﴿And those of blood relationship﴾ meaning the kinsfolk, ﴿are closer to one another﴾ in inheritance, ﴿in the Book of Allah, than the believers and the emigrants﴾, meaning in inheritance by virtue of faith and emigration, which was at the beginning of Islam, but it was abrogated (naskh). ﴿Except﴾ but ﴿that you do to your allies a kindness﴾ by way of a bequest, which is permissible. ﴿That was﴾, meaning the inheritance by faith and emigration was abrogated by the inheritance of those of blood relationship, ﴿in the Book inscribed﴾. By "the Book" in both places is meant the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

﴿And﴾ mention ﴿when We took from the prophets their covenant﴾ at the time they were brought forth from the loins of Adam like *dharr* (the plural of *dharrah*, meaning the smallest ants). ﴿And from you, and from Noah, and Abraham, and Moses, and Jesus son of Mary﴾, [to take the covenant] that they should worship God and call others to His worship. Mentioning these five is *min 'atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm* (the specific being listed after the general, as a conjunction of the particular upon the general). ﴿And We took from them a firm covenant﴾, meaning a strong one, to fulfil what they were entrusted with, and this was the oath by God, the Exalted. Then He took the covenant.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 8:

﴿That He may ask the truthful about their truthfulness﴾ (i.e., Allah will question the messengers) regarding their conveying of the message, as a rebuke to the disbelievers who denied them. ﴿And He has prepared﴾ (by Him, Exalted is He) ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ (among them, i.e., those who denied the prophets) ﴿a painful punishment﴾ (causing pain). It is coordinated with (ʿatf ʿala) "We took" (in the previous verse).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 33, verse 9:

﴿O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when there came to you soldiers [i.e., the disbelievers, confederates] and We sent upon them a wind and soldiers you did not see﴾ [i.e., angels]. ﴿And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing﴾ [with the "ta'" (ta) reading, referring to the digging of the trench; and with the "ya'" (ya) reading, referring to the confederation of the polytheists].

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 10:

﴿When they came upon you from above you and from below you﴾ from the upper part of the valley and its lower part, from the east and the west. ﴿And when the eyes shifted﴾ they turned away from everything else toward their enemy from every side. ﴿And the hearts reached the throats﴾ "hanajir" is the plural of "hanjara," which is the end of the windpipe (al-hulqum), from the intensity of fear. ﴿And you were thinking about Allah with various thoughts﴾ differing regarding victory and despair.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 11:

﴿There, the believers were tested﴾ they were put to the test, so that the sincere might be distinguished from others ﴿and were shaken with a severe shaking﴾ they were moved, ﴿a severe shaking﴾ due to the intensity of the terror.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 12:

﴿And﴾ remember ﴿when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ [i.e., weakness of belief] ﴿said: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion"﴾ [i.e., of victory], ﴿false﴾ [i.e., vain].

And when a group of them said, [i.e., the hypocrites], "O people of Yathrib [Yathrib is the land of Madinah; it is not made diptote for being a place-name and conforming to the verbal pattern], there is no station for you [pronounced with a damma and with a fatha on the mim: i.e., there is no staying and no standing], so return [to your homes in Madinah]." They had gone out with the Prophet (ﷺ) to Sal', a mountain outside Madinah, for fighting. And a faction of them asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for permission [to return], saying, "Indeed our houses are exposed," unprotected and feared for. "But they are not exposed," [the negation is from] "they only intend to flee" from fighting.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 14:

﴿And if it had been entered upon them from its sides﴾ — i.e., the city, from its regions (nawahiha), ﴿then they had been asked to commit fitnah﴾ — i.e., those who entered asked them to commit fitnah, which is shirk, ﴿they would have given it﴾ — with the madd and the qasr (two readings: lengthened and shortened alif), i.e., they would have given it, and done it.
﴿And they had certainly made a covenant with Allah before this, that they would not turn their backs [in flight]. And the covenant of Allah will be questioned.﴾ About fulfilling it.
Say: "Fleeing will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing, and then you will not be given enjoyment [in this world] except for a little" — the remainder of your appointed terms.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 17:

﴿Say, "Who is it that can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm,"﴾ that is, who can grant you refuge from Allah, ﴿or if He intends for you mercy?﴾ [who can harm you if Allah intends for you good]; ﴿and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector﴾ i.e., other than Him, ﴿who will benefit them﴾ ﴿or any helper﴾ who will repel harm from them.

Note on the translation: the source gloss reads "هَلاكًا وهَزِيمَة" (destruction and defeat) after "سُوءًا", and "يُصِيبكُمْ بِسُوءٍ إنْ أرادَ اللَّه بِكُمْ خَيْرًا" appears after "أوْ"; the Qur'anic text ﴿أَوْ أَرَادَ بِكُمْ رَحْمَةً﴾ is rendered above as "mercy," with the gloss given in brackets as the commentary's paraphrase.

Qur'anic quotations go in ﴿ ﴾ with plain meaning inside. Technical terms like tafsir are transliterated with a gloss on first mention.

﴿Indeed, Allah knows those among you who hinder others﴾ (al-mu'awwiqin), meaning those who discourage [others from fighting], ﴿and those who say to their brothers, "Come here to us!"﴾ (halumma), meaning come over, ﴿and they do not come to battle﴾ (al-ba's), meaning fighting, ﴿except a little﴾, meaning for show and to be heard of.

﴿Being niggardly towards you﴾ with help. It is the plural of *shaḥīḥ* (stingy, grudging), and it is a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) referring to the pronoun in *yatūna* (they come). ﴿So when fear comes, you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who swoons from the agony of death.﴾ The comparison is to the gaze of, or the rolling of the eyes of, one who ﴿swoons from the agony of death﴾, meaning its throes. ﴿Then when fear departs﴾ and the spoils have been gathered, ﴿they lash you﴾, that is, they harm you or strike you, ﴿with sharp tongues, being niggardly towards the good﴾, meaning the spoils, which they seek to obtain. ﴿Those have not believed﴾ in truth, ﴿so Allah has nullified their deeds﴾. ﴿And that nullification is ever easy for Allah﴾, by His will.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 20:

﴿They think the confederates﴾ of the disbelievers ﴿have not withdrawn﴾ to Makkah, out of their fear of them. ﴿And if the confederates should come﴾ again, ﴿they would wish﴾ they could ﴿be [living] among the Bedouins﴾, that is, dwelling in the desert, ﴿asking about your news﴾, your reports, concerning the disbelievers. ﴿And even if they were among you﴾ this time, ﴿they would not fight except a little﴾, out of show and out of fear of being reproached.

﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah there is for you an excellent example﴾. The word إسْوَة is read with a kasra and with a damma on the hamza (إسْوَة and أُسْوَة). حَسَنَة means: to be followed (iqtida') by him in fighting and in steadfastness in its positions. ﴿for whoever﴾: لِمَن is a badal (a grammatical substitute, in which a noun replaces an earlier one) for لَكُمْ. ﴿hopes for Allah﴾ means fears Him, ﴿and the Last Day, and remembers Allah much﴾, unlike whoever is not like that.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 22:

﴿When the believers saw the confederates﴾ among the disbelievers, ﴿they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us"﴾ of trial and victory, ﴿and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth﴾ in the promise, ﴿and it increased them only in faith﴾ that is, in affirmation of Allah's promise ﴿and submission﴾ to His command.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 23:

﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they pledged to Allah.﴾ [They were true] in steadfastness alongside the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿Among them is one who has fulfilled his vow﴾ — he died or was killed in the way of Allah.

﴿And among them is one who awaits﴾ that [same fate].

﴿And they have not changed [their pledge] at all﴾ in the covenant, unlike the state of the hypocrites.

﴿That Allah may reward the truthful for their truthfulness﴾ and punish the hypocrites, ﴿if He wills﴾, by causing them to die in their hypocrisy, ﴿or relent toward them. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ to whoever repents, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 25:

﴿And Allah repelled those who disbelieved, in their rage, not having obtained any good﴾ — i.e., the confederates (al-Ahzab) — ﴿their aim of victory over the believers﴾ — ﴿And Allah sufficed the believers in fighting﴾ — by the wind and the angels — ﴿And Allah is ever Powerful﴾ — over bringing into being whatever He wills — ﴿Exalted in Might﴾ — prevailing over His affair.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 26:

﴿And He brought down those of the People of the Scripture who supported them from their fortresses﴾, i.e., the Qurayzah, ﴿from their fortresses﴾, their strongholds, the plural of ṣayṣah (fortress), which is that by which one fortifies oneself. ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾, the fear, ﴿a group you killed﴾ of them, and they were the fighting men, ﴿and you took captive a group﴾ of them, i.e., the descendants (dhurriyyah, offspring, women and children).

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And He made you inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not yet trodden.﴾

Tafsir text: "بَعْد" (ba'd, "afterwards") — and it is Khaybar, which was taken after Qurayza.

Translation:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 27:

﴿And He made you inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and a land you had not yet trodden.﴾ [After it] — and it is Khaybar, which was taken after Qurayza.

O Prophet, say to your wives: (Ayah quoted) "O Prophet, say to your wives, if you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you (the provision of divorce) and release you with a fair release" — 

Translating the passage as it stands:

"O Prophet, say to your wives" (﴿يا أيّها النَّبِيّ قُلْ لِأَزْواجِك﴾). They were nine, and they asked him for some of the adornments of the world which he did not have.

"If you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you" (﴿إنْ كُنْتُنَّ تُرِدْنَ الحَياة الدُّنْيا وزِينَتها فَتَعالَيْنَ أُمَتِّعكُنَّ﴾), that is, the provision of divorce.

"And I will release you with a fair release" (﴿وأُسَرِّحكُنَّ سَراحًا جَمِيلًا﴾): I will divorce you without harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 29:

﴿And if you desire Allah and His Messenger and the Final Abode﴾, i.e., Paradise, ﴿then indeed Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you﴾ by desiring the Final Abode ﴿a great reward﴾, i.e., Paradise. So choose the Final Abode over the worldly life.

﴿O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a manifest indecency, the punishment will be doubled for her, twice over.﴾ Read with a fatha and with a kasra on the ya' (in ﴿مُبَيَّنَة﴾), meaning either that it has been made manifest (bayyanat) or that it is itself manifest (bayyinah). ﴿Yudā'af﴾ (is doubled), and in another reading (qira'ah) it is ﴿yuḍa''af﴾ with a shaddah, and in another ﴿nuḍa''if﴾ with a nun together with it. ﴿Al-'adhāb﴾ (the punishment) is in the accusative. ﴿Lahā al-'adhābu ḍi'fayn﴾ (for her the punishment is twice over): twice the punishment of others besides them, meaning double its like.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 31:

﴿Whoever of you submits﴾ obeys ﴿to Allah and His Messenger, and does righteous deeds, We will give her her reward twice﴾ i.e., double the reward of other women. And in another reading, with the ya' (third person) in "ta'mal" and "nu'tiha" (wa-ya'mal, wa-yu'tiha).

﴿And We have prepared for her a generous provision﴾ in Paradise, in addition.

O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any one of other women (ka-ahadin ka-jama'atin) among women, if you are godfearing (in-ittaqaytunna) toward God, for you are greater (fa-innakunna a'zam). So do not be soft in speech (fa-la takhda'na bil-qawl) toward men, lest he in whose heart is a disease (fayatma'a alladhi fi qalbihi maradun) — hypocrisy (nifaq) — should be drawn to desire you. And speak a fair speech (wa-qulna qawlan ma'rufan), without softness.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 33, verse 33:

﴿And remain﴾ (with the vowel on the qaf read both with a kasra and with a fatha) ﴿in your houses﴾ from qarar (staying, settling). Its original form was aqrirna (with the vowel on the ra read both with a kasra and with a fatha), from qararta (with the vowel on the ra read both with a fatha and with a kasra). The vowel of the ra was transferred to the qaf, and the hamzat al-wasl (the connecting hamza) was dropped with it. ﴿And do not display yourselves﴾ by dropping one of the two taa's from its original form, ﴿like the display of the former Jahiliyyah﴾ (the Age of Ignorance), meaning what was before Islam, of women showing their adornments to men. The display after Islam is mentioned in the verse ﴿and not display their adornment except that which appears thereof﴾. ﴿And establish prayer, and give zakah, and obey Allah and His Messenger. Indeed, Allah intends to remove from you the impurity﴾, meaning the sin, O ﴿people of the household﴾, meaning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and purify you﴾ from it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 34:

﴿And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah﴾ the Qur'an ﴿and the wisdom﴾ the Sunnah ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Subtle﴾ toward His friends ﴿Acquainted﴾ with all His creation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 35:

﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women, the believing men and the believing women, the obedient men and the obedient women,﴾ (al-Qanitin, meaning) those who are obedient (al-Mutiʿat), ﴿the truthful men and the truthful women﴾ in faith, ﴿the patient men and the patient women﴾ in acts of obedience, ﴿the humble men﴾ (al-Mutawadiʿin, meaning) those who are humble, ﴿and the humble women, the charitable men and the charitable women, the fasting men and the fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who guard them﴾ against what is unlawful, ﴿the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Him—Allah has prepared for them forgiveness﴾ for their sins ﴿and a great reward﴾ for acts of obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 36:

﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ (read with the taa' and the yaa': "yakūna" and "takūna"). ﴿Al-khiyarah﴾ means al-ikhtiyar (choice) ﴿in their affair﴾, in contrast to the command of Allah and His Messenger. It was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Jahsh and his sister Zaynab, whom the Prophet proposed for marriage to Zayd ibn Harithah. They disliked that, when they knew, because they had thought beforehand that the Prophet had proposed her for himself. Then they were content, after the verse [was revealed]. ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error﴾ (manifest, clear). So the Prophet ﷺ married her to Zayd. Then his gaze fell upon her after a while, so her love fell into his heart, and Zayd's aversion to her [fell into his heart]. Then he said to the Prophet ﷺ: "I wish to divorce her." He said: ﴿Keep your wife to yourself﴾.

﴿وإذْ﴾ (wa-idh, "and when") is in the accusative case, governed by ﴿اذْكُرْ﴾ (udhkur, "remember"). ﴿وإذْ تَقُول لِلَّذِي أنْعَمَ اللَّه عَلَيْهِ﴾ means: "And when you said to the one on whom Allah bestowed favor" with Islam, ﴿وأَنْعَمْت عَلَيْهِ﴾ "and you bestowed favor on him" by manumission. He was Zayd ibn Harithah, who had been among the captives of the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) bought him before the ba'tha (the sending as a prophet), freed him, and adopted him. ﴿أمْسِكْ عَلَيْك زَوْجك واتَّقِ اللَّه﴾ means: "Keep your wife to yourself and fear Allah," regarding the matter of divorcing her. ﴿وتُخْفِي فِي نَفْسك ما اللَّه مُبْدِيه﴾ means: "and you concealed within yourself what Allah was to disclose," that is, bring to light, of your love for her and that if Zayd divorced her, you would marry her. ﴿وتَخْشى النّاس﴾ means: "and you feared the people," lest they say, "He married his son's wife." ﴿واللَّه أحَقّ أنْ تَخْشاهُ﴾ means: "while Allah has more right that you fear Him," in every matter. He married her, and there is no blame on you for what people say. Then Zayd divorced her, and her iddah (waiting period) ended. ﴿فَلَمّا قَضى زَيْد مِنها وطَرًا﴾ means: "So when Zayd had accomplished his need from her," ﴿زَوَّجْناكها﴾ "We married her to you." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon her without permission, and he fed the Muslims bread and meat. ﴿لَكَيْ لا يَكُون عَلى المُؤْمِنِينَ حَرَج فِي أزْواج أدْعِيائِهِمْ إذا قَضَوْا مِنهُنَّ وطَرًا﴾ means: "so that there would be no discomfort for the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they had accomplished their need from them." ﴿وكانَ أمْر اللَّه﴾ means: "and the command of Allah was," that is, His decree, ﴿مَقْضِيّه﴾ "carried out."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 38:

﴿There is no restriction upon the Prophet in what Allah has made lawful for him﴾ (ahalla); ﴿Allah's way﴾ (sunnah Allah), i.e., like the way of Allah, so it is in the accusative by removal of the preposition, ﴿with those who passed on before﴾ from among the prophets, that there is no restriction upon them in that, as a widening for them in marriage; ﴿and the command of Allah is a decree decreed﴾ (fi'luhu), i.e., a judgment decided.

﴿Alladhīna﴾ is a qualifier (*naʿt*, an adjective describing the noun it follows) of "alladhīna" before it: ﴿who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him, and fear none except Allah﴾, so they do not fear the talk of people concerning what Allah has made lawful for them. ﴿And Allah is sufficient as Reckoner﴾, a guardian over the deeds of His creation and their reckoning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 40:

﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men﴾, so he is not the father of Zayd, that is, his (biological) father, and so it is not forbidden for him to marry his wife Zaynab. ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets﴾, so there will not be, after him, a son of a man who is a prophet. And in another recitation (qira'ah) with a fat-ha on the ta' (khatam), meaning an instrument of sealing (khatam): that is, through him the prophets were sealed. ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾, of Him being that there is no prophet after him. And when the Master (al-Sayyid) 'Isa descends, he will judge by his law (shari'ah).
{Wa sabbihuhu bukratan wa asīlā} — "And glorify Him at dawn and at dusk": at the beginning of the day and at its end.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 43:

﴿He it is Who sends His blessings upon you﴾, i.e., has mercy upon you, ﴿and His angels [too]﴾ ask forgiveness for you, ﴿that He may bring you out﴾ — that He may continue bringing you out — ﴿from the darknesses﴾, i.e., disbelief, ﴿into the light﴾, i.e., faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 44:

﴿Their greeting﴾ from Him, the Exalted, ﴿on the day they meet Him will be: "Peace"﴾ in the tongue of the angels, ﴿and He has prepared for them a generous reward﴾, which is Paradise.

O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness (شاهدًا) over those to whom you were sent, and as a bringer of good news (ومبشرًا) of Paradise to those who believe in your truthfulness, and as a warner (ونذيرًا) warning those who denied you of the Fire.
"And as one who summons to Allah" to His obedience "by His permission" by His command, "and as a illuminating lamp" meaning, like one in being guided by him.
﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾: it is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 48:

﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾ in what opposes your Sharia; ﴿and disregard﴾ leave off ﴿their harm﴾; do not requite them for it until you are commanded regarding them with a command; ﴿and put your trust in Allah﴾, for He is sufficient for you; ﴿and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ entrusted to Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 49:

﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is not for you any waiting period [due] from them that you should count. So provide for them and release them in a fine manner.﴾

And in another recitation: "tumāssūhunna" (تُماسُّوهُنَّ), meaning: you have intercourse with them (tujāmi'ūhunna).

﴿Then there is not for you any waiting period [due] from them that you should count﴾: you count it (tuḥṣūnahā) by menstrual periods (bil-aqrā') and other than them.

﴿So provide for them﴾: give them (a'ṭūhunna) that which they may enjoy (mā yastamti'na bihi), i.e., if no bridal gift (ṣadaqa) has been specified for them. Otherwise, they are due only half of the specified amount (niṣf al-musammā) alone. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, and al-Shafi'i held to it.

﴿And release them in a fine manner﴾: let them go their way (khallū sabīlahunna) without harm (min ghayr iḍrār).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 50:

﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal payments (ujur) you have given﴾ (i.e., their dowries, muhur) ﴿and what your right hand possesses of those whom Allah has given you as spoils (fa'a) from the disbelievers, by captivity, such as Safiyya and Juwayriyya﴾ ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you﴾ (this excludes those who did not emigrate) ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet, if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾ seeking to take her in marriage without a dowry ﴿—a privilege for you alone, apart from the believers﴾ the marriage by the wording of gifting (hiba) without a dowry ﴿We know what We have enjoined upon them﴾ i.e., the believers ﴿concerning their wives﴾ of the rulings, namely that they should not exceed four wives, and should not marry except with a guardian (wali), witnesses and a dowry ﴿and what their right hands possess﴾ of female slaves, by purchase or other means, on condition that the slave girl be of those who are lawful for her owner, such as a kitabiyya (Christian or Jewish woman), unlike a Magian or idolatress, and that she be purified (istibra') before intercourse ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾ (la-kay) relates to what precedes this ﴿in marriage﴾ (haraj: narrowness/constraint in marriage) ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ regarding what is difficult to avoid ﴿Merciful﴾ by granting latitude in that.﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 51:

﴿Turjī﴾ (you may postpone), with a hamza or with a yā' in its place: tu'akhkhir (you defer) ﴿whom you will of them﴾, i.e., of your wives, from her turn (nawba) ﴿and you may take to yourself whom you will﴾ of them, tu'wī (you draw in, take to yourself), so that you go to her ﴿and whomever you desire﴾ talabta (you seek) ﴿of those you have set aside﴾ from the division (qisma) ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ in seeking her and taking her to yourself. It is better in that matter, after the division had been obligatory for him. ﴿That﴾ choice ﴿is more fitting﴾, closer ﴿that their eyes may be comforted, and they may not grieve, and that they may be content with what you have given them﴾, that which the one given the choice has mentioned, ﴿all of them﴾, an emphasis on the subject in yarḍayna (they may be content). ﴿And Allah knows what is in your hearts﴾ of the matter of the women and the inclination toward some of them. Indeed We gave you this choice concerning them only as an ease for you in everything you wish. ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing﴾ of His creation, ﴿Forbearing﴾ regarding their punishment.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 52:

﴿It is not lawful for you [to marry]﴾ (read with both the taa' and the yaa'), ﴿women after [this]﴾, after the nine whom you have chosen (for marriage), ﴿nor [is it lawful] that you exchange them﴾, by dropping one of the two taa's in the original (i.e., tatabaddala becoming tabaddala), ﴿for [other] wives﴾, by divorcing them, or some of them, and marrying another in place of the one you divorced, ﴿even though their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses﴾, of the slave-women, for these are lawful to you. The Prophet (ﷺ) did possess, after them, Mariyah, who bore him Ibrahim, and he died during his lifetime. ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful﴾, Preserver (ḥafīẓan) [of all things].

﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you﴾ for entry, by invitation, ﴿to a meal﴾, so that you enter ﴿without waiting for its readiness﴾, waiting for ﴿its cooking﴾ (its ripeness), a verbal noun (maṣdar) of the verb أنِيَ يَأْنِي (anā ya'nī). ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse, and do not linger﴾ remaining ﴿seeking familiar conversation﴾ with one another. ﴿Indeed, that [lingering]﴾ ﴿was troubling the Prophet, so he would be shy of you﴾ to have you leave. ﴿But Allah is not shy of the truth﴾ to have you leave; that is, He does not abandon stating it. It is also read as يَسْتَحْيِ with a single yāʾ (ي). ﴿And when you ask them﴾, that is, the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾ a partition. ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾ from doubtful thoughts. ﴿And it is not for you to trouble the Messenger of Allah﴾ in any way, ﴿nor to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that﴾ was ﴿in the sight of Allah﴾ a sin.

If you disclose a thing or conceal it (﴿If you disclose a thing or conceal it﴾) concerning their marrying (nikah) after him, (﴿then indeed Allah is ever Knowing of all things﴾) and so He will recompense you for it.

No blame on them regarding their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, or their women (i.e., the believing women), nor those whom their right hands possess (of female slaves and male slaves) that they may be seen by them and speak to them without a veil. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding what you have been commanded. ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, nothing being hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet﴾ Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace (salaam)﴾, i.e., say: "O Allah, send blessings upon our master Muhammad, and grant him peace."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 57:

﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger﴾ — they are the disbelievers, who ascribe to Allah what is exalted above Him, such as offspring and partners, and who deny His Messenger. ﴿Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter﴾ — He has removed them far away. ﴿And He has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ — one bringing humiliation, and it is the Fire.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 58:

﴿Those who hurt believing men and believing women without their having earned it﴾ accuse them of what they did not do, ﴿have certainly borne a slander﴾ they have taken upon themselves a lie, ﴿and a clear sin﴾ evident.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 59:

﴿O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the women of the believers: let them draw their outer garments (jalabib) over themselves.﴾ Jalabib is the plural of jilbab, which is the wrap (mula'ah) with which a woman covers herself. That is, they should let some of it down over their faces when they go out for their needs, except for one eye. ﴿That is more suitable﴾ closer ﴿to their being recognized﴾ as free women ﴿so that they will not be harmed﴾ by being molested. This is in contrast to slave women, who do not cover their faces. The hypocrites used to molest them. ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ of what has passed of them in terms of leaving off covering ﴿and Merciful﴾ toward them, since He has concealed them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 60:

﴿La-in﴾ (the lam is a lam of oath) ﴿lam yantahi al-munafiqun﴾ (the hypocrites do not desist) from their hypocrisy ﴿wa-alladhina fi qulubihim maradh﴾ (and those in whose hearts is a disease) by fornication ﴿wal-murjifun fi al-madinah﴾ (and those who spread false rumours in Medina) among the believers, by their saying: "The enemy has come upon you, and your detachments have been killed or defeated" ﴿la-nughriyannaka bihim﴾ (We will surely set you against them) that is, We will give you power over them ﴿thumma la yujawiruna-ka﴾ (then they will not remain as your neighbours) that is, they will not dwell with you ﴿fiha illa qalilan﴾ (in it, except for a little) then they will be expelled.

Cursed (مَلْعُونِينَ): removed far away from mercy. ﴿Wherever they are found﴾ (أيْنَما ثُقِفُوا): wherever they are come upon (وُجِدُوا). ﴿They shall be seized and killed with a (thorough) killing﴾ (أُخِذُوا وقُتِّلُوا تَقْتِيلًا): that is, the ruling concerning them is this, given in the form of a command to do it.

﴿The way of Allah﴾, i.e., Allah has ordained that ﴿concerning those who passed away before﴾, from the earlier nations, ﴿concerning their hypocrites, the rumour-mongers, the believers﴾. ﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾ from Him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 63:

﴿Men ask you﴾ (i.e., the people of Makkah) ﴿about the Hour﴾, when it will occur. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah. And what would make you know?﴾ (i.e., will inform you) ﴿about it?﴾ meaning: you do not know it. ﴿Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ (i.e., it will exist).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 64:

﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers﴾ — He has removed them (abʿadahum, i.e., banished them far from mercy) — ﴿and has prepared for them a blaze﴾ — a fierce fire which they will enter.

Abiding therein forever (khalidin): [their] abiding is predestined (muqaddaran khuluduhum) ﴿therein forever. They will not find any protector (waliyyan)﴾ who would guard them from it, ﴿nor any helper (nasiran)﴾ who would repel it from them.
﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh!"﴾ The "yā" is for alerting (tanbīh, calling attention).

﴿And they will say﴾, that is, the followers among them, ﴿"Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters﴾ (sādatanā). It is read in another reading as ﴿sādātanā﴾, which is the plural of a plural (jam' al-jam', a plural formed from a plural form). ﴿and our senior leaders, and they led us astray from the way﴾, the way of guidance."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 68:

﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment from the Fire﴾, meaning twice Our punishment. ﴿And curse them﴾, meaning punish them, ﴿with a great curse﴾, meaning a multiple curse. In another recitation it is read with the single letter ba' (as kabīran, "great"), meaning a great [curse].

﴿O you who have believed, do not be⁠ like those who harmed Moses⁠﴾ with their statement, as a proverb: "Nothing prevents him from bathing with us except that he has an *adar*." ﴿But Allah cleared him of what they said⁠﴾ by his placing his garment on a stone to bathe, and the stone fled with his garment until it stopped among a group of the Children of Israel. Moses pursued it, took his garment, and covered himself with it. They saw him, and there was no *udra* on him. *Udra* is a swelling in the testicle. ﴿And he was distinguished in the sight of Allah⁠﴾, meaning, possessing standing.

Among the ways our Prophet ﷺ was harmed: he distributed a share, and a man said, "This is a distribution by which the Face of Allah, the Exalted, was not intended." The Prophet ﷺ became angry at that and said: "May Allah have mercy on Moses. He was harmed with more than this, and he was patient." Narrated by al-Bukhari.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 70:

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ Correct (ṣawāban).

﴿He will set right for you your deeds﴾, meaning He will accept them, ﴿and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great success﴾, meaning he has attained a desired goal.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 72:

﴿Indeed, We offered the trust﴾ — the prayers and other obligations, in which there is reward for performing them and punishment for neglecting them — ﴿to the heavens and the earth and the mountains﴾ — by creating in them understanding and speech — ﴿but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it﴾ — they feared it — ﴿and man bore it﴾ — Adam, after it had been offered to him — ﴿Indeed, he was a wrongdoer to himself﴾ — by bearing what he bore — ﴿ignorant﴾ — of it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 33, verse 73:

﴿So that Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women﴾ The lam (of purpose) is connected to "We offered" (ʿaradnā), which is followed by "the bearing of the trust by Adam", ﴿those who waste the trust﴾; ﴿and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and the believing women﴾ who discharge the trust; ﴿and Allah is ever Forgiving﴾ toward the believers, ﴿Merciful﴾ to them.
